about: What cannot be scored from [Fock] here, one record each: claim, mechanism, evidence, asserted_value, source. See felizjueves.literature.limits. Milestone 12 scores no published cell: there is no tables.json in this directory, by decision (pin 2).

limits.claim: No [Fock] table is a scoreboard here. In the text read (arXiv v1), Tables 1 and 2 are single-A100 Fock-build speedups of opt-Brc and opt-UM over TeraChem, QUICK and GPU4PySCF; Table 3 is single-iteration K timings in seconds on a V100 against LibintX; Table 4 is SCF iteration timings in seconds on 1 and 4 A100s. Milestone 12's 'Table 3, A100 seconds' is the journal version's numbering, which this reading could not see; the preprint's Table 4 fits that description, and the conclusion is the same for every table.
limits.mechanism: Every table is a wall-clock measurement (or a ratio of two) of whole programs on hardware this box does not have: an A100 or a V100, against an RTX 3080 (sm_86) and an RX 9060 XT (gfx1200). A timing depends on the card, the compiler and the rest of the program, none of which a reconstruction of §3 describes, so no model or kernel here predicts one.
limits.evidence: Table captions of arXiv:2407.21445v1, read for this record (#271). Milestone 12 pin 2: one literature file, no table cells; no tables.json is added under data/literature/fock/, and test/test_fock_coverage.py holds that.

limits.claim: §6's benchmarks (Figs. 5-9: single-GPU comparisons, strong scaling on 1-4 A100s, CPU comparisons, J/K scaling and per-class timings) are not reproduced or scored.
limits.mechanism: They are whole-program wall-clock on NERSC Perlmutter nodes (AMD EPYC 7763, four A100 40 GB or 80 GB), against other packages this repo does not run. This repo builds the two-electron F of §3's kernel, not an SCF program, and has neither the hardware nor the comparators.
limits.evidence: §6's opening paragraph and figure captions, arXiv:2407.21445v1 (#271).

limits.claim: There is no published register table for the §3.2 kernel: the paper reports no register count, spill figure or occupancy for any opt-Brc class, so milestone 12's generated F kernel has no published figure to be held to. The predecessor's hand-spelled kernel (its test/hgp/brc/ptxas_data.py, measured under nvcc 13.0, -arch=sm_86) is a quality baseline of common ancestry (#289), never a witness and never a [Fock] cell.
limits.mechanism: Registers and spills are compiler readings of one kernel text on one architecture; the paper prints only timings, and mentions registers only qualitatively (§2.3's register pressure; §6's 80 GB cards 'to accommodate' f-function spills).
limits.evidence: A search of arXiv:2407.21445v1 for 'register' finds §2.3, §4.2, §4.3.2, §4.4 and §6 prose and no table (#271); the predecessor records the same absence.

limits.claim: Milestone 12 moves no [JEngine] cell, floor, claim or status. [Fock] was already a reference here (docs/references.md entry 23), cited as prior art in eri/k_exchange/k.py and kernel_k.py ([Fock, §4.3.1], [Fock, §4.3.2]); this directory is the first time a section of it is reconstructed rather than cited, and its records are its own.
limits.mechanism: [JEngine] is J only and its board is Tables 1-3 of that paper; [Fock] §3 is another engine (HGP, fused F) with no table cell this repo can score. The two registries are checked per paper (felizjueves.literature.claims.load_registry), so neither reads the other's records.
limits.evidence: #271 adds data/literature/fock/ and touches no file under data/literature/jengine/ or data/scoreboards/; test/test_claims.py checks each paper's registry separately.

limits.claim: The efficacy of §3.2's screens (eq. 29's pre-launch batch-pair screen and the six-block in-kernel screen) is not measured: how much work they remove depends on how extended the molecule is, and every fixture here is compact.
limits.mechanism: A Schwarz or density screen removes quartets in proportion to the fraction of distant pairs; in H2, H2O and HF that fraction is small, so a measured saving would be a fact about the fixture, not about the screen (milestone 12 pin 9). An extended case is a follow-up.
limits.evidence: Milestone 12 pin 9; the fixture list in test/oracle/fixtures/. #291 asserts fock/prelaunch-screening-removes-launches on its MECHANISM only (the removed batch pairs are never launched and hold no quartet with G_ab G_cd >= tau; test/test_fock_pairs.py), and this record is why the efficacy half is not asserted with it.

limits.claim: The pair stream (#285) counts what its screens remove on the compact fixtures and compares nothing: how many contracted pairs are deleted, how many primitive pairs are pruned and how many batch pairs eq. 29's pre-launch screen removes are recorded below, and none of them is a measurement of the screens' efficacy. At tau = 1e-10 no batch pair is removed before launch on any fixture, while primitive pruning already fires on 6-31G and cc-pVDZ.
limits.mechanism: Eq. 29's screen removes a batch pair only when both magnitudes are small, i.e. when the pairs' Schwarz factors G_ab decay below tau^(1/n); in H2 and H2O every shell pair overlaps (the smallest contracted G_ab is above 0.02 on every fixture), so the screen cannot fire at an SCF threshold, and the fraction it removes at a loose tau is a fact about the fixture (milestone 12 pin 9). Pruning acts inside a pair (a tight primitive against a diffuse one) and is less sensitive to the molecule's extent, so it fires here, and by splitting contraction degrees it ADDS batches. The follow-up is an extended case -- #88's chain of four H2 (data/ao/screening.json) or a longer one -- with the eq. 29 and six-block screens' removals counted against the unscreened F of eri/fock/fock.py.
limits.evidence: launch_f.f_launches with ao.pairs.primitive_schwarz_bounds under reference.pq.one_centre, n = 2, on the tracked fixtures named below; test/test_fock_pairs.py recomputes every count and asserts that the screened batch pairs hold no ERI >= tau.

limits.claim: The cross-tree ptxas baseline (#289, data/measured/fock_baseline.json) is a quality baseline of common ancestry, never a numeric witness: it puts the generated F kernel's sm_86 registers, spill bytes and stack frame beside the predecessor's hand-spelled kernel's frozen PTXAS_MEASURED rows, under the predecessor's flags, and no correctness claim may cite it. It carries no threshold, no ratchet and no pass/fail on any delta.
limits.mechanism: Milestone 12 was designed from the predecessor's checkout, so the two kernels are not independent: where they agree, the agreement may be the shared design and not the physics, and a register count says nothing about a value in any case. Correctness is witnessed only from outside -- eri.fock.fock's every-ordered-quartet sweep and libcint's vj/vk through the tracked fixtures (pin 6, pin 10). A tolerance on the deltas would turn a finding into a green test, so the file records them and the only structural reading is where the register ceiling falls: inside L = 3 there (ds|ps fits, pp|ps spills), between L = 3 and L = 4 here, with pp|ps the one class that crossed.
limits.evidence: data/measured/fock_baseline.json (its about, boundary and reading); test/test_fock_baseline.py holds the a >= b to la <= lb mapping a bijection on the eleven cells, the boundary recomputed from the rows, and each unit's source hash, and its cuda cases re-compile each unit under -dc -O2 --std=c++17 -arch=sm_86 and compare. Milestone 12's description: 'a quality baseline, never a numeric witness (same ancestry)'.

limits.claim: Which side of [Fock]'s symmetry-versus-screening trade gives up less -- full 8-fold symmetry with a six-block density screen (§3, opt-Brc), or every ordered quartet with a one-block screen (§4, opt-UM) -- is not decided here (fock/symmetry-vs-screening, UNVERIFIABLE).
limits.mechanism: The trade is settled by wall-clock, and [Fock]'s is whole-program timings on A100 (and V100) cards; a screen's payoff also grows with how extended the molecule is. This box has an RTX 3080 (sm_86) and an RX 9060 XT (gfx1200), every fixture is compact, and nothing has been timed. Milestone 14 removed the confound milestone 12 had: its two cells differed in the recurrence as well as the scheme (HGP fused against MMD split), but the (HGP, split) cell now exists (Target.J and Target.K on Engine.HGP, kernel_hj / kernel_hk), so the HGP row holds both schemes on one recurrence and a timing of Target.F against HGP Target.J + Target.K would not confound the two decisions the paper itself says it confounds (§1, §4.3). That timing is not made (#331): the store refuses an HGP J/K row (measured_store.HGP_JK_REFUSED), and the split cell ran on the RTX 3080 only.
limits.evidence: What is held is structural, in claims.json's reason for fock/symmetry-vs-screening: Target.F reads six weighted density blocks and any one can keep a quartet (test/test_kernel_f.py), Target.J and Target.K visit every ordered quartet (test/test_ao_fock.py) and Target.J's screen reads one block (test/test_kernel.py). What would settle it on our cards: the fused F and the split J + K builds timed end to end behind the card gate on both cards, over an extended molecule set (a follow-up, pin 9), on one recurrence: HGP fused (Target.F) against HGP split (milestone 14; test/test_hjk_build.py and test/test_hjk_ondevice.py hold its J and K to the ordered sweep and libcint), so the scheme is not confounded with the recurrence. [Fock]'s own conclusion needs an A100 and its benchmark set.

limits.claim: What milestone 12's fused F does not reach (#293). It is the two-electron G = J - K/2 of one density, built once per call on the 21-class ladder (every shell l <= 2, up to (dd|dd)): no f or higher shell reaches the HGP engine, nothing is kept on the card across SCF iterations, there is no gradient, no lever (measured_store refuses a lever on an F key) and no batch count other than 1 (spec._F_BATCH_REFUSAL). The bra record is staged into shared memory per thread, not cooperatively, so section 3.2's staging bandwidth is not reproduced. Milestone 12 built neither off-diagonal cell of the paper's 2x2. The split HGP J/K was built by milestone 14 (the next record); the fused MMD F does not exist.
limits.mechanism: Each is a scope decision of milestone 12, not a defect of the paper. Pin 3 fixes the ladder at l <= 2, and on sm_86 whether a class fits its registers follows its HRR boundary count (hgp.vrr.target_set): every class with at most 40 targets fits and every class with 76 or more spills (#290), while (ff|ff)'s set is 5,476 against (dd|dd)'s 961. Pin 4 makes n_batches = 1 because an HGP class has no Hermite targets to partition. Pin 1 keeps the split HGP J/K out of section 3, and the fused MMD F was never in scope. The IR has no barrier (ir/__init__.py), so a cooperative load cannot be spelled. kernel_f.MAX_PRIM_PAIRS = 128 is a refusal past the cap, never an overflow.
limits.evidence: hgp.vrr.CLASSES and test/test_hgp_vrr.py (the 21 classes); emit's --fock-l accepts 0..2 and --fock-class refuses a class off the ladder (test/test_emit_fock.py, test/test_emit_cli.py); test/test_spec_f.py (the batch refusal); test/test_measured.py (an F key with a lever is refused); kernel_f.py's docstring, 'THE STAGING IS PER THREAD, BECAUSE THE IR HAS NO BARRIER'; data/measured/kernels.json's 42 F rows (#288, #290). The follow-ups are filed: #325 (split HGP J/K, closed into milestone 14, which built it), #326 (fused MMD F), #330 (f and above), #333 (a barrier and the cooperative staging).

limits.claim: What milestone 14's split HGP J/K does not reach (#409). It is Target.J and Target.K on Engine.HGP: every ordered quartet visited once and deposited at weight 1, in two class modes (canonical: one kernel per 8-fold orbit through a runtime perm; ordered: one per class, the `ordered` lever), with one density block screened per build, a skip and never a break. Nothing above L = 4 is tested: the 70 ordered classes and 17 orbits with L <= 4 are interpreted and run, and the goldens stop at shell l <= 2 (50 ordered classes and 13 orbits, 126 units per backend). Nothing is timed or stored, nothing is kept on the card across SCF iterations, n_batches is 1 and `ordered` is the only lever. It ran on the RTX 3080 only; on the RX 9060 XT it is compiled only. The screens' efficacy is unmeasured, and the fused MMD F, the 2x2's last cell, does not exist.
limits.mechanism: Each is a scope decision of milestone 14 or a fact of this box, not a defect of the paper. Every test is capped at L <= 4 (the milestone's run limit), though the builders and the emitter accept any L. measured_store refuses an HGP J/K row (HGP_JK_REFUSED) until the issue that times these kernels admits the row, its cells and its header together, as #278 did for F. An HGP class has no Hermite targets to partition, so the builders refuse n_batches != 1. The RX 9060 XT was not enumerated by kfd, so its device run is attached to #431 by the user's decision. The fixtures are compact, so a screen's removals would be a fact about the fixture (pin 9, #329).
limits.evidence: test/test_hgp_orbits.py (50 / 13 at shell l <= 2 and 70 / 17 uncapped at L <= 4; the index map exact and eri/eri.py within 1e-12 of the summed scale, worst 2.6e-16; PR #469); test/test_spec_engine.py (PR #470); test/test_hjk_pairs.py (PR #471); test/test_kernel_hj.py and test/test_kernel_hk.py (all 70 classes, both modes, interpreted; PRs #473, #474); test/test_emit_hjk.py (126 goldens per backend, compiled under nvcc sm_86 and hipcc gfx1200; PR #475); test/test_hjk_build.py (H2/STO-3G, H2O/STO-3G and H2O/6-31G interpreted, worst 3.82e-15 of the scale against libcint; cc-pVDZ not run; PR #476); test/test_hjk_ondevice.py (RTX 3080: 184 passed, worst 5.90e-16 of the scale against the host and 2.59e-15 against libcint; HIP compile-only, 182 passed; PR #477).
